text:
Jamal: quick one — bigBank wants a 6-week on‑prem POC in a walled‑garden datacenter. Only monthly 2hr maintenance windows, USB transport allowed, and they require minimal downtime. Need: feasibility, upgrade cadence we can guarantee, SOW outline, and answers for their security questionnaire by EOW. Can we do this?
Alex: short answer: yes, with caveats. We should use small delta bundles (minibundles) + a staging validation step. Full image swaps will be too risky in a 2hr window.
Maria: agree. Proposed flow: 1) initial full bootstrap via signed USB image; 2) subsequent deltas applied during window; 3) a quick preflight that runs locally (<5m). Rollback must be single-command and tested.
Rohan: security note — customer requires signed artifacts, HSM-backed signing or equivalent, and attestations for supply chain. We'll provide an answers doc for the questionnaire but need to confirm key custody approach (we can't hold customer keys).
Jamal: @Maria can you outline the runbook bullet points we need to include in the SOW? Also @Rohan, which questionnaire sections need redlines?
Maria: runbook bullet points: - preflight checksum + disk space check - stop local inference service - apply delta bundle - verify model signature + kv-cache integrity - smoke test (3 prompts) - verify latency SLA - rollback if smoke fails (auto revert). Keep it lightweight for the 2hr window.
Maria: sample preflight command we propose for the customer:
```
redwoodctl preflight --bundle /mnt/usb/minidelta.tar.gz --check-disk --check-deps
```
Alex: packaging detail — delta bundles will ship as a tar.gz containing manifest.json and layer diffs. We avoid kernel/driver changes in POC. If they need infra-level updates we schedule a separate ops window.
Rohan: questionnaire redlines: - Key management (Q12) — we state customer-managed KMS + agent attestation. - Artifact signing (Q7) — we provide CI signing with detachable signature verification. - Data exfil (Q19) — we provide network isolation details and logs export policy. I'll draft precise language.
Emily: pricing side — for a 6‑week POC we can offer: 50% off hosted list on Dedicated reserved, plus 2 dedicated support engineers for the onboarding week (remote) included. Additional oncall during monthly windows billed at hourly rate. I'll put numbers in the SOW draft.
Jamal: do we need a legal addendum for offline media acceptance? customer asked about liability if USB is compromised.
Rohan: yes, addendum: customer accepts physical media chain of custody; we provide signed checksums and verification steps. We can offer to validate checksums remotely during bootstrapping but we can't certify courier integrity.
Maria: ops constraint — delta size target <= 200MB to fit their internal transfer policy. If delta >200MB we need approval and a larger window. Also note: model quantization changes are not allowed mid‑POC (they change outputs).
Alex: engineering note — to keep deltas small we recommend caching static tokenizer/model shards and only shipping kv-cache deltas and small weights updates. We'll supply a compatibility matrix for model versions and runtime (will need customer's runtime/os kernel minor version).
DeployBot: minibundle created 1749999200 by ci/minibuilder v2; signature: sha256:abc123...; status: signed.
Jamal: perfect. Next steps: Maria to draft runbook + maintenance script examples, Rohan to draft security questionnaire answers and addendum wording, Emily to draft SOW/pricing. I'll bundle these into a single deliverable to customer by Friday. :thumbsup:
Emily: noted — I'll include a clause for two one‑hour dry‑run sessions before the first maintenance window (free).
Rohan: I'll mark the Qs that need legal signoff and ping legal if any redlines touch export controls.
Maria: I'll aim to have the runbook + sample commands in PR by tomorrow afternoon.
Jamal: thanks team — I'll update the customer and loop in procurement after we have draft SOW.
